chunks: Ahmad ibn Isha narrated from Musa ibn Abd al-Malik and al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, and Musa ibn Abd al-Malik from a man who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man having intercourse with his wife from behind, so he said: 'A verse from the Book of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, made it permissible: the saying of Lut (Lot): "Here are my daughters, they are purer for you." And he knew that they did not desire the private part.'

key_terms.الْفَرْجَ: the private part / genitalia (specifically male in this context)
key_terms.قَوْلُ لُوطٍ: the saying of Lot (referring to the Quranic verse)

ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic evidence for the permissibility of intercourse from behind in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) derives the permissibility of vaginal intercourse from behind by interpreting Prophet Lut’s offer of his daughters in Surah Hud as a contextual clue; he notes that Lut knew the mob sought the 'farj' (genital organ) generally, implying the female organ was included in that general term. This hadith is significant in Shia jurisprudence for establishing that the act is not restricted to the front position, relying on the linguistic flexibility of the term 'farj' in the Quranic narrative.
